html:
Ethane conformations
The right-hand pair is fixed in the eclipsed (60°) geometry. The slider rotates the rear carbon of the left molecule so you can watch staggered turn into eclipsed.
staggered 0° → eclipsed 60°  (H–C–C–H torsion 60°)
Torsional strain (left): 0.0 kJ/mol
Guided steps
Eclipsing interactions (right molecule)
Click one H–H pair on the right — a brace, the H letters or the spheres — to isolate a single 4.0 kJ/mol interaction.
Drag to orbit: the ball-and-stick models turn in 3D (the left one starts end-on down the C–C bond) while the flat Newman projections stay face-on. Reset View returns to the printed view.
⚠ Figure failed to load

elements: LEFT PANEL (always staggered, fixed reference): Newman projection — thin black open circle = rear carbon
LEFT PANEL: solid black dot at circle center = front carbon
LEFT PANEL: three heavy black front-carbon bonds from the center dot outward at screen angles 90° (up), 210° (down-left), 330° (down-right)
LEFT PANEL: three thinner rear-carbon bonds from the circle rim outward at 30°, 150°, 270°
LEFT PANEL: three green 'H' letters at the ends of the front bonds
LEFT PANEL: three magenta 'H' letters at the ends of the rear bonds

LEFT PANEL: ball-and-stick ethane viewed end-on — dark gray front carbon sphere, rear carbon sphere just behind/below it, three green H spheres (front) and three dark-red H spheres (rear) alternating in a hexagonal ring
Bold caption 'Ethane—staggered conformation' centered beneath the left Newman + model pair
CENTER: straight horizontal reaction-style arrow pointing right
CENTER: arrow label text 'Rotate rear carbon 60°' set above the arrow
RIGHT PANEL (eclipsed by default): Newman projection — circle, center dot, three heavy front bonds at 90°, 210°, 330°
RIGHT PANEL: three thinner rear-carbon bonds lying directly under the front bonds (also 90°, 210°, 330°) so bonds superimpose
RIGHT PANEL: three green 'H' and three magenta 'H' letters in overlapping pairs (green drawn slightly offset/above magenta so both read)
RIGHT PANEL: three curly braces, one straddling each eclipsed H–H pair (top, lower-left, lower-right)
RIGHT PANEL: three '4.0 kJ/mol' labels, one beside each brace
RIGHT PANEL: ball-and-stick ethane end-on with green and dark-red hydrogen spheres in coincident pairs (tripod appearance)
Bold caption 'Ethane—eclipsed conformation' centered beneath the right Newman + model pair
Optional small readout beneath the right panel: torsion angle and total strain (3 × 4.0 = 12 kJ/mol)

interactions.teaches: The right-hand conformation is the left one with the rear carbon turned: dragging back from 60° (eclipsed, default) to 0° returns it to the staggered geometry shown on the left, so the learner sees the two textbook panels are two frames of one continuous rotation while the left reference panel never changes.
interactions.label: Right panel: rear-carbon rotation from staggered (0° staggered → 60° eclipsed)

interactions.teaches: Each of the three eclipsing H–H interactions costs the same 4.0 kJ/mol; clicking one pair isolates its two hydrogens, its brace and its label, showing that 3 × 4.0 = 12 kJ/mol is the whole rotational barrier.

Turning the ball-and-stick models off the end-on axis reveals that the Newman circle is simply the C–C bond seen down its length, and that eclipsed hydrogens are genuinely aligned in 3D rather than merely overlapping on paper.

demo_steps.title: The two conformations side by side
demo_steps.narration: Left: staggered ethane — green (front) and magenta (rear) hydrogens alternate 60° apart. Right: eclipsed ethane — each rear bond hides behind a front bond, and the three braces each cost 4.0 kJ/mol, 12 kJ/mol in total.

demo_steps.title: Un-rotate the right carbon
demo_steps.narration: Drag the right panel's rear carbon back to 0° and it becomes identical to the left panel: the braces vanish because no hydrogens are aligned. The two figures are one molecule at two torsion angles.

demo_steps.title: Halfway: strain building
demo_steps.narration: At 30° the magenta hydrogens have swung a third of the way onto the green ones; in the model the red spheres slide toward the green spheres and torsional strain climbs toward its maximum.

demo_steps.title: Back to eclipsed — count the interactions
demo_steps.narration: Return to 60°. Click any brace to isolate one H–H eclipsing interaction: three identical 4.0 kJ/mol penalties add to the 12 kJ/mol barrier to rotation about the C–C bond.

plan.geometry_notes: LOAD STATE: both halves visible at once, left = staggered (static, never driven by any control), right = eclipsed (slider default 60°). Layout on a common horizontal baseline across ~16 world units: left Newman centered at x=-6.2, left ball-and-stick at x=-3.4, arrow spanning x=-1.6→+1.6 at y=0, right Newman at x=+3.4, right ball-and-stick at x=+6.2. Captions in bold dark gray at y=-3.2, centered at x=-4.8 ('Ethane—staggered conformation') and x=+4.8 ('Ethane—eclipsed conformation'); caption font ~0.42 u tall. Newman geometry: rear-carbon circle radius 1.15 u, black stroke #1a1a1a width 0.045; front carbon filled black dot radius 0.11; three heavy front bonds width 0.11 from dot to radius 1.8 at 90°, 210°, 330°; three rear bonds width 0.055 from circle rim (r=1.15) to radius 1.8, at 30°/150°/270° when the panel's rotation = 0° and rotating clockwise to 90°/210°/330° at 60°. Left panel is permanently at 0°; right panel angle = slider value. 'H' letters ~0.45 u tall, bold: front green #1f9e57, rear magenta #E0218A, placed at radius 2.05 along each bond; when a green and magenta H coincide, offset the magenta letter 0.18 u radially outward so both stay legible. BALL-AND-STICK (end-on, C–C axis toward camera, separate the two carbons slightly in screen space by tilting the pair ~8°): carbon spheres radius 0.55 dark gray #3f3f3f, rear carbon drawn slightly smaller/dimmer behind; hydrogen spheres radius 0.42 — front three bright green #3fbf55, rear three dark red #9e2b1e; sticks light blue-gray #b8c2cc radius 0.11; C–C 1.54 u, C–H 1.10 u, H–C–C 109.5° so hydrogens project to a ring of screen radius ~1.5 u; left model hydrogens form an alternating hexagon (60° apart), right model shows three coincident green/red pairs (tripod), red spheres peeking just outside the green ones. BRACES: three black curly braces (stroke 0.04) with span 1.0 u, sitting just outside each overlapped H pair at 90°, 210°, 330° of the RIGHT Newman only, each with a '4.0 kJ/mol' label (font ~0.34 u, #333) placed radially outboard. Braces and labels are fully visible by default and for any right-panel angle ≥ 45°; below 45° they fade out linearly reaching 0 opacity at 35°. ARROW: black shaft 0.06 u thick, head 0.35 u, with two-line bold label 'Rotate rear carbon 60°' (font ~0.36 u) centered above the shaft. HIGHLIGHT STATE: selected pair's brace, label, both H letters and both spheres glow (white rim, +40% brightness); all other panel content dims to 35% opacity. Energy relation: E(θ) ≈ 6.0 (1 + cos 3θ_torsion)/... use simply 12 kJ/mol × (1 + cos(3×(60−slider)°))/2 — 0 kJ/mol at slider 0 (staggered), 12 kJ/mol at slider 60 (eclipsed); optional readout '3 × 4.0 = 12 kJ/mol' under the right caption. Background white.
plan.notes: Keep the left Newman + left model as a fixed group with no bindings to any control, so the source's left panel geometry can never drift. Only the right rear-carbon group receives the slider quaternion, and it is initialized to 60° before the first frame is drawn. Render Newman projections as flat screen-facing geometry (CSS2D/overlay or billboarded planes) using Line2 thick-line material so the heavy/thin bond contrast survives; orbit affects only the two ball-and-stick groups (shared camera orbit around their local axes), never the flat projections or text. Curly braces from quadratic Bézier Line2 strips, billboarded. Depth-sort and z-offset coincident spheres with a thin dark outline so eclipsed pairs stay distinguishable. All text via CSS2DRenderer with generous font sizes (captions bold ~20px, H letters bold ~18px, kJ/mol ~15px at default zoom) and DPI-aware scaling; clamp the camera so the full 16-unit-wide layout fills ≥75% of the frame width.

authoredPrompt: This figure compares two conformations of ethane, each shown as a Newman projection paired with a ball-and-stick model, with a reaction-style arrow between them. On the left, the Newman projection draws the front carbon as a dot at the center of a circle with three heavy bonds radiating up, down-left, and down-right to hydrogens lettered in green, while the rear carbon is the circle itself with three thinner bonds emerging at the left, right, and bottom to hydrogens lettered in magenta, so the two sets alternate evenly. Its ball-and-stick model, viewed end-on, shows a dark gray carbon ringed by three green and three red spheres in alternating positions. The horizontal arrow between the halves is labeled "Rotate rear carbon 60°". On the right, the projection shows each front bond lying directly over a rear bond, so the green and magenta hydrogens appear in overlapping pairs, and three curly braces, one at each pair, are each labeled "4.0 kJ/mol". The matching model now shows the green and red spheres in coincident pairs. Bold labels read "Ethane—staggered conformation" and "Ethane—eclipsed conformation". Setting the two projections side by side makes the hydrogen spacing the thing being compared, and the three equal energy labels partition the rotational barrier into individual eclipsing interactions.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the rear carbon from 0 to 60 degrees; the Newman projection and ball-and-stick model update continuously from staggered to eclipsed, making torsional alignment the source of the conformational change.
- Click for highlighting one eclipsed H-H pair; its brace and 4.0 kJ/mol label brighten along with the overlapping hydrogens, clarifying how three identical interactions add to the rotational barrier.
authoredContext:
Despite what we’ve just said, we actually don’t observe perfectly free rotation in ethane. Experiments show that there is a small (12 kJ/mol; 2.9 kcal/mol) barrier to rotation and that some conformations are more stable than others. The lowest-energy, most stable conformation is the one in which all six C–H bonds are as far away from one another as possible—staggered when viewed end-on in a Newman projection. The highest-energy, least stable conformation is the one in which the six C–H bonds are as close as possible—eclipsed in a Newman projection. At any given instant, about 99% of ethane molecules have an approximately staggered conformation and only about 1% are near the eclipsed conformation.

Staggered conformation of ethane undergoes rotation of rear carbon 60 degrees to form eclipsed conformation of ethane.

The extra 12 kJ/mol of energy present in the eclipsed conformation of ethane is called torsional strain. Its cause has been the subject of controversy, but the major factor is an interaction between C–H bonding orbitals on one carbon and antibonding orbitals on the adjacent carbon, which stabilizes the staggered conformation relative to the eclipsed one. Because a total strain of 12 kJ/mol arises from three equal hydrogen–hydrogen eclipsing interactions, we can assign a value of approximately 4.0 kJ/mol (1.0 kcal/mol) to each single interaction. The barrier to rotation that results can be represented on a graph of potential energy versus degree of rotation, in which the angle between C–H bonds on the front and back carbons as viewed end-on (the dihedral angle) goes full circle from 0 to 360°. Energy minima occur at staggered conformations, and energy maxima occur at eclipsed conformations, as shown in the figure.
sourceQmd: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 3: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry

demo_steps.title: Staggered ethane
demo_steps.narration: Front bonds point up, down-left and down-right; rear bonds bisect them at left, right and bottom. Green (front) and magenta (rear) hydrogens alternate evenly — 60° apart — the lowest-energy conformation.

demo_steps.title: Rotating the rear carbon
demo_steps.narration: Turning the rear carbon 30° swings the magenta hydrogens toward the green ones; in the model the red spheres slide toward the green spheres and torsional strain begins to build.

demo_steps.title: Eclipsed ethane
demo_steps.narration: At 60° each rear bond lies directly behind a front bond. The three braces mark three eclipsing H–H interactions, each worth 4.0 kJ/mol — 12 kJ/mol total. Click a pair to isolate one interaction.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Layout mirrors the source: a Newman projection on the left of the frame and its ball-and-stick model immediately to its right, both centered on a common horizontal baseline; captions in bold below. Newman: rear-carbon circle radius 1.0 world unit, thin black stroke (#1a1a1a, ~0.03 u); front carbon a filled black dot radius 0.09 at the center; three thick front bonds (~0.09 u wide) from the dot outward to length 1.6 at screen angles 90° (up), 210° (down-left), 330° (down-right); three thinner rear bonds (~0.05 u) starting at the circle rim and extending to radius 1.6, at 30°, 150°, 270° when the slider is 0 (staggered) and rotating clockwise toward 90°, 210°, 330° at slider 60 (eclipsed). Front 'H' letters green (#1f9e57), rear 'H' letters magenta (#E0218A), placed just beyond each bond end. Ball-and-stick: C–C axis pointing at the camera; carbon spheres radius 0.45, dark gray (#4a4a4a) with specular highlight; hydrogen spheres radius 0.30 — front three green (#3fbf55) with lighter rim, rear three dark red (#9e2b1e); bonds are light blue-gray cylinders (#b8c2cc) radius 0.09. C–C length 1.54 u, C–H length 1.10 u, H–C–C angle 109.5°, so hydrogens splay outward from the C–C axis by ~70° from the far direction; front hydrogens project to screen angles 90/210/330°, rear hydrogens to 30/150/270° when staggered and rotate to coincide when eclipsed. Torsion angle = 60° − slider value. Braces (eclipsed state only) are thin black curly braces of span ~0.8 u sitting just outside each overlapped H pair at 90°, 210°, 330°, each with a '4.0 kJ/mol' label in dark gray; brace and label opacity fade in linearly as the slider passes 40→60. Highlighted pair: brace, label and both hydrogen spheres/letters brighten (yellow-white glow, others dimmed to ~35% opacity). Arrow between panels: straight horizontal black arrow ~2.5 u long with two-line label 'Rotate rear carbon 60°' above it; the arrow's progress can echo the slider. Background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the Newman projection as flat screen-space geometry (orthographic overlay or a billboarded plane) so it never tilts with orbit; restrict orbit to the ball-and-stick model group. Use Line2/thick line material for the Newman bonds so the front/rear line-weight contrast survives; use MeshPhysicalMaterial with mild roughness plus a soft key light for the CPK spheres to match the glossy textbook rendering. Curly braces built from quadratic Bézier tube/Line2 strips, billboarded. Depth-sort so front hydrogens draw over rear ones when eclipsed; add a slight z-offset and a subtle outline on the green spheres so coincident pairs remain readable. Labels via HTML/CSS2DRenderer for crisp text. Slider drives a single quaternion rotation of the rear-carbon group about the C–C axis, shared by both the Newman and 3D representations so they stay in lockstep.

discrepancies: Default state shows the right-hand pair in the STAGGERED geometry (slider at 0°) even though it is captioned 'Ethane—eclipsed conformation', so at first glance the figure presents two identical staggered Newman projections/models — the source's side-by-side staggered vs. eclipsed contrast is lost until the user moves the slider.

The three curly braces and the three '4.0 kJ/mol' annotations — a defining feature of the source's right panel — are invisible at the default state (opacity fades in only between 40° and 60°), so the energy annotation is absent in the initial view.
The whole composition renders quite small in the canvas with large empty margins; Newman circles, H letters and captions are noticeably smaller/lighter than the bold typography of the source.

Ball-and-stick models: the two carbons are drawn nearly superimposed and the spheres are small relative to bond lengths, so the characteristic hexagonal 'star' (staggered) and tripod (eclipsed) silhouettes of the source photographs read less clearly; front carbon is not visually distinguished in front of the rear one.

Rear hydrogens in the models use a dark brick red while the source rear spheres are a brighter red; front-carbon dot/heavy bonds in the Newman drawing are thinner than the source's very heavy black bonds.
evaluation.notes: Composition, color coding and the rotation concept are captured well with a genuinely useful slider/step/highlight interaction set, but the default state leaves the right-hand 'eclipsed' pair drawn as staggered with its braces and 4.0 kJ/mol labels hidden, which undercuts the figure's central staggered-vs-eclipsed comparison.
action_items: Make the right-hand panel and model render the eclipsed (60°) geometry by default — either initialize the slider/step at 60° or decouple the right pair so it always shows the eclipsed state while the slider animates a separate demonstration.
Show the three braces and '4.0 kJ/mol' labels whenever the right panel is at/near eclipsed (and by default), rather than only fading in above 40°.
Increase overall scale (larger heightFraction / tighter layout) and bump font sizes for the H letters, kJ/mol annotations and bold captions to match the source's weight and improve legibility.
Enlarge hydrogen/carbon spheres and separate the two carbons slightly in screen space so the ball-and-stick models read as the hexagonal (staggered) and tripod (eclipsed) views in the source.
plan_action_items: Specify that the source's two states must be simultaneously visible at load (left = staggered, right = eclipsed) with the interactive rotation as an additional exploration rather than the source of the right panel's geometry.

feedback.rationale: The core structural issue is that the plan ties the right-hand 'eclipsed' panel to the shared rotation slider so the source's simultaneous staggered-vs-eclipsed contrast (and its brace/energy annotations) is absent at load, which requires re-specifying the interaction decomposition rather than mere rendering tweaks.

plan.notes: Keep the left Newman + left model as a fixed group with no bindings to any control, so the source's left panel geometry can never drift. discrepancies: The two bottom '4.0 kJ/mol' labels on the eclipsed Newman sit on top of the braces/H letters (the text overlaps the lower-right brace and the magenta H), whereas in the source they are clearly offset outside the braces.

The left ball-and-stick model in the source is drawn essentially end-on down the C–C bond so the six hydrogens form a clean regular hexagon around a single visible carbon; here the tilt (elevation 14°) separates the two carbons and squashes the hexagon, making the staggered relationship less obvious.

The right ball-and-stick model in the source reads as a compact tripod with the rear (dark red) hydrogens hidden directly behind the green ones; the generated version shows both carbons side-by-side with the red spheres well clear of the green, so the 'eclipsed = hidden behind' cue is weaker.
Overall composition is framed small within the canvas with a large empty band below the captions, so the figure occupies noticeably less of the view than the source's tightly-cropped strip.
evaluation.notes: Faithful reproduction of both Newman projections, both ball-and-stick models, the reaction arrow, braces and captions with correct green/magenta/red colour coding, backed by a genuinely useful dihedral slider, guided steps and per-pair highlighting; main weaknesses are label/brace overlap on the eclipsed side and ball-and-stick viewing angles that read less cleanly as staggered vs eclipsed than the source.

CENTER: straight horizontal reaction-style arrow pointing right
CENTER: arrow label text 'Rotate rear carbon 60°' set above the arrow
RIGHT PANEL (eclipsed by default): Newman projection — circle, center dot, three heavy front bonds at 90°, 210°, 330°
RIGHT PANEL: three thinner rear-carbon bonds lying directly under the front bonds (also 90°, 210°, 330°) so bonds superimpose
RIGHT PANEL: three green 'H' and three magenta 'H' letters in overlapping pairs (green drawn slightly offset/above magenta so both read)

interactions.teaches: The right-hand conformation is the left one with the rear carbon turned: dragging back from 60° (eclipsed, default) to 0° returns it to the staggered geometry shown on the left, so the learner sees the two textbook panels are two frames of one continuous rotation while the left reference panel never changes.
interactions.label: Right panel: rear-carbon rotation from staggered (0° staggered → 60° eclipsed)

interactions.teaches: Each of the three eclipsing H–H interactions costs the same 4.0 kJ/mol; clicking one pair isolates its two hydrogens, its brace and its label, showing that 3 × 4.0 = 12 kJ/mol is the whole rotational barrier.

Turning the ball-and-stick models off the end-on axis reveals that the Newman circle is simply the C–C bond seen down its length, and that eclipsed hydrogens are genuinely aligned in 3D rather than merely overlapping on paper.

demo_steps.title: The two conformations side by side
demo_steps.narration: Left: staggered ethane — green (front) and magenta (rear) hydrogens alternate 60° apart. Right: eclipsed ethane — each rear bond hides behind a front bond, and the three braces each cost 4.0 kJ/mol, 12 kJ/mol in total.

demo_steps.title: Un-rotate the right carbon
demo_steps.narration: Drag the right panel's rear carbon back to 0° and it becomes identical to the left panel: the braces vanish because no hydrogens are aligned. The two figures are one molecule at two torsion angles.

demo_steps.title: Halfway: strain building
demo_steps.narration: At 30° the magenta hydrogens have swung a third of the way onto the green ones; in the model the red spheres slide toward the green spheres and torsional strain climbs toward its maximum.

demo_steps.title: Back to eclipsed — count the interactions
demo_steps.narration: Return to 60°. Click any brace to isolate one H–H eclipsing interaction: three identical 4.0 kJ/mol penalties add to the 12 kJ/mol barrier to rotation about the C–C bond.

In the source the right-hand ball-and-stick model is a clearly eclipsed tripod seen with the front carbon toward the viewer and the three red H peeking directly behind the green ones; the generated right model is tilted so that the C–C axis and sphere overlap pattern read less clearly as eclipsed.
